$comment: Rule catalog — fitness. Contains exactly the eleven fitness prohibitions from the source specification, plus six rules about what a fitness plan must record. Counts are pinned in artifacts/rule-inventory.json; each prohibition's description reproduces the source's own line verbatim and is checked by scripts/fidelity.mjs.

rules.title: Training through sharp or significant injury pain is never recommended
rules.description: Never recommend training through sharp/significant injury pain
rules.rationale: Sharp pain is a signal that something is being damaged, and training through it converts a recoverable problem into a lasting one. The distinction from ordinary training discomfort is well understood by people who train and routinely blurred by systems that encourage persistence as a virtue.
rules.remediation: Distinguish training discomfort from injury pain, and where the signal is sharp or significant, advise stopping and — where it persists — evaluation by someone qualified to assess it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Training load is never increased indefinitely without recovery
rules.description: Never increase training load indefinitely without recovery
rules.rationale: Adaptation happens during recovery, not during the session. A monotonically rising load is not a faster version of progressive overload — it is the removal of the mechanism that makes overload work, and it ends in injury, illness, or abandonment rather than in fitness.
rules.remediation: Build recovery into the progression: lighter periods, planned deloads, and a ceiling that is reconsidered rather than assumed.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment. The related requirement fitness.recovery-planned checks only that a Recovery and Rest section exists.

rules.title: Maximum effort is never treated as inherently superior
rules.description: Never treat maximum effort as inherently superior
rules.rationale: Most training adaptations come from accumulated work at sustainable intensities, and maximum effort has a recovery cost that limits how much of it is useful. Treating it as inherently better inverts the ratio that actually produces progress, and it selects for people who can tolerate punishment rather than people who improve.
rules.remediation: Match intensity to the adaptation being sought, and say why a given intensity was chosen rather than defaulting to harder.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Fitness is never judged from one workout
rules.description: Never judge fitness from one workout
rules.rationale: A single session reflects sleep, food, stress, heat, and where in the week it fell at least as much as it reflects fitness. Judging from one is the trend-over-event failure in its most demoralising form: a bad day gets read as a loss of fitness, and the plan is rewritten around noise.
rules.remediation: Assess progress from trends across sessions, and treat any single workout as one observation among them.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Heart rate alone is never treated as a complete measure of exercise quality
rules.description: Never treat heart rate alone as a complete measure of exercise quality
rules.rationale: Heart rate is one signal, and it moves on heat, hydration, caffeine, sleep, illness, and stress independently of training. It also says nothing at all about the things much of training is for — force production, movement quality, skill. Optimising the number optimises the proxy.
rules.remediation: Read heart rate alongside perceived effort, the work actually performed, and the goal of the session.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Intensity is never prescribed without considering baseline and context
rules.description: Never prescribe intensity without considering baseline/context
rules.rationale: The same prescription is trivial for one person and injurious for another. Intensity is meaningful only relative to current capacity, and a prescription issued without it is a guess presented as a plan — with the error falling hardest on the least trained, who are least able to recognise it.
rules.remediation: Establish current capacity and relevant context first, and express intensity relative to it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment. The related requirement fitness.baseline-recorded checks only that a Baseline section exists.

rules.title: Unsafe progression is never encouraged solely to hit a target
rules.description: Never encourage unsafe progression solely to hit a target
rules.rationale: A target is a means to an outcome, and progression that risks injury to reach it defeats the outcome it was chosen to serve. Dates chosen for convenience are especially prone to this: the deadline is arbitrary and the injury is not.
rules.remediation: Where the safe rate of progression will not meet the target, move the target. Say so explicitly rather than compressing the plan.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Soreness is never equated with workout effectiveness
rules.description: Never equate soreness with workout effectiveness
rules.rationale: Soreness tracks novelty and eccentric load, not adaptation. It is highest when someone is least trained and fades as they improve, so using it as a quality signal rewards constant change over the consistency that actually produces progress.
rules.remediation: Judge effectiveness by the work performed and by progress over time; treat soreness as information about novelty and recovery.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Exhaustion is never equated with workout quality
rules.description: Never equate exhaustion with workout quality
rules.rationale: Exhaustion measures how depleted someone is, which is a cost rather than a benefit. A session can be exhausting and useless, or comfortable and highly productive. Treating depletion as the goal produces training that cannot be sustained and, in aggregate, less of it.
rules.remediation: Define what each session is for and judge it against that, not against how depleted it left the person.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Missed workouts are never punished with excessive compensatory exercise
rules.description: Never punish missed workouts with excessive compensatory exercise
rules.rationale: Compensating for a missed session concentrates load exactly when readiness is lowest, which is when injury risk is highest. It also frames training as a debt to be repaid, and that framing is what turns one missed session into abandonment — the real threat to a training plan is not the missed workout, it is the response to it.
rules.remediation: Resume the plan at the point it reached. A missed session is absorbed, not repaid.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: Extreme exercise volumes are never recommended merely for faster results
rules.description: Never recommend extreme exercise volumes merely for faster results
rules.rationale: Volume produces adaptation only to the extent it can be recovered from, and past that point additional volume produces fatigue, injury, and dropout instead. Speed is the usual justification, and it is the one that does not survive contact with the outcome: the fastest sustainable rate beats a faster rate that ends in a layoff.
rules.remediation: Set volume from what can be recovered from and sustained. Where more speed is wanted than that allows, say what the ceiling is rather than raising the volume.
rules.$assuranceNote: Judgment; reports not-evaluated without a recorded human review.

rules.title: A fitness plan exists and states its goals
rules.description: Training is guided by a written plan that states what it is for, rather than assembled session by session with the goal held implicitly.
rules.rationale: Without a stated goal every prescription is unfalsifiable — no session can be wrong for a plan that never said what it was aiming at. A written goal is also what makes it possible to notice when the training has drifted away from it.
rules.remediation: Write the plan into artifacts/fitness-plan.md using the fitness-plan template, beginning with a Goals section.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the plan exists and has a Goals section. It establishes nothing about whether the goals are appropriate or the plan is sound.

rules.title: The fitness plan records baseline fitness
rules.description: The plan records the starting point it was built from: current capacity, relevant training history, and any limitations.
rules.rationale: Baseline is what makes intensity meaningful and progress measurable. Recording it also dates it — a baseline from a year ago is visibly a baseline from a year ago, whereas an unrecorded one is silently assumed to still hold.
rules.remediation: Add a Baseline section recording current capacity, relevant history, and limitations.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty — never that the baseline is accurate or current.

rules.title: The fitness plan documents its progression scheme
rules.description: The plan states how load progresses: what increases, by how much, on what trigger, and what happens when the trigger is not met.
rules.rationale: An undocumented progression becomes 'add a little each time', which has no stopping rule and no response to a bad week. Writing down the trigger is what allows the plan to hold when things do not go well, which is when a plan is actually needed.
rules.remediation: Add a Progression section stating what increases, by how much, on what trigger, and what happens when progress stalls.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty. Whether the progression is safe is fitness.no-load-increase-without-recovery, which no machine evaluates.

rules.title: The fitness plan includes recovery and rest provisions
rules.description: The plan states its recovery and rest provisions: rest days, lighter periods, planned deloads, and what to do when recovery is inadequate.
rules.rationale: Recovery is where adaptation happens, and a plan that leaves it unstated leaves it to be sacrificed first whenever the schedule tightens. Writing it in makes it part of the plan rather than the slack in it.
rules.remediation: Add a Recovery and Rest section covering rest days, lighter periods, and the response to inadequate recovery.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty — never that the recovery provision is adequate for the load.

rules.title: The fitness plan includes a pain and injury response protocol
rules.description: The plan states in advance what to do when pain appears: how to tell training discomfort from injury pain, when to stop, and when to seek evaluation.
rules.rationale: The decision to stop is made worst in the moment, by someone who is invested in finishing. Deciding the rule beforehand, when nothing is at stake, is what makes it followable when something is.
rules.remediation: Add a Pain and Injury Response section distinguishing discomfort from injury pain and stating the stopping and escalation rules.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty. Whether the protocol is correct is fitness.no-training-through-sharp-pain, which no machine evaluates.

rules.title: The fitness plan defines a trend-based review cadence
rules.description: The plan states when it will be reviewed and on what evidence — a period over which trends are assessed, rather than a reaction to whatever the last session showed.
rules.rationale: A plan with no review cadence gets reviewed whenever something feels wrong, which is precisely when the evidence is a single bad session. Fixing the cadence in advance is what makes trend-based assessment the default rather than the exception.
rules.remediation: Add a Review Cadence section stating the review period and the trends that will be assessed.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector establishes that the section is present and non-empty — never that reviews actually happen or that they are trend-based.
